source_evidence.observation: The inherited setting fixes independent sub-gaussian random variables X_1,...,X_N with zero means and unit variances, an arbitrary coefficient vector a=(a_1,...,a_N) in R^N, and K=max_i ||X_i||_{psi_2}.
The displayed conclusion is c(K)(sum_{i=1}^N a_i^2)^(1/2) <= ||sum_{i=1}^N a_i X_i||_{L^1} <= (sum_{i=1}^N a_i^2)^(1/2).
The source repeats K=max_i ||X_i||_{psi_2} and requires c(K)>0 to be a quantity that may depend only on K.
The suggested proof is to establish ||Z||_{L^2} <= ||Z||_{L^1}^{1/4} ||Z||_{L^3}^{3/4}, apply it to Z=sum_i a_i X_i, and bound ||Z||_{L^3} using Exercise 2.6.5 at p=3.
The book calls a random variable sub-gaussian when it satisfies one of Proposition 2.5.2's equivalent properties and defines ||X||_{psi_2}=inf{t>0 : E exp(X^2/t^2)<=2}.

binders: A finite indexed list X_1,...,X_N of random variables, with the index range i=1,...,N inherited from Exercise 2.6.5 (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchor: opening sentence of Exercise 2.6.5).
A coefficient vector a=(a_1,...,a_N) in R^N, with no restriction on its entries (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchor: opening sentence of Exercise 2.6.5).
The parameter K=max_{1<=i<=N} ||X_i||_{psi_2} (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchor: the 'where K' sentence of Exercise 2.6.5 and the 'Here K' sentence of Exercise 2.6.6).
A positive lower-comparison quantity c(K), whose permitted dependence is only on K (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchor: sentence following the Exercise 2.6.6 display).
hypotheses: X_1,...,X_N are independent (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchor: opening sentence of Exercise 2.6.5, inherited by 'in the setting of Exercise 2.6.5').
Every X_i is sub-gaussian (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchor: opening sentence of Exercise 2.6.5).
Every X_i has mean zero (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchor: phrase 'with zero means' in Exercise 2.6.5).
Every X_i has variance one (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchor: phrase 'unit variances' in Exercise 2.6.5).
conclusions: For the weighted sum Z=sum_{i=1}^N a_i X_i, c(K)(sum_{i=1}^N a_i^2)^(1/2) <= ||Z||_{L^1} <= (sum_{i=1}^N a_i^2)^(1/2) (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchor: displayed inequality in Exercise 2.6.6).
definitions_and_conventions: The Euclidean coefficient size in the comparison is (sum_{i=1}^N a_i^2)^(1/2) (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchor: both ends of the Exercise 2.6.6 display).
The middle expression is the L^1 norm of the random variable sum_{i=1}^N a_i X_i (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchor: middle of the Exercise 2.6.6 display).

The sub-gaussian norm used to define K is the book's ||.||_{psi_2}; Definition 2.5.6 gives ||X||_{psi_2}=inf{t>0 : E exp(X^2/t^2)<=2} (PDF page 16; printed page 27; anchor: Definition 2.5.6 and equation (2.13)).
The upper comparison constant is exactly 1, while the lower comparison constant is the positive quantity c(K) (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchor: Exercise 2.6.6 display and following sentence).
implicit_context: The phrase 'in the setting of Exercise 2.6.5' imports its family, independence, sub-gaussianity, zero-mean, unit-variance, coefficient-vector, and K assumptions; it does not import p as a new binder because Exercise 2.6.6 fixes the L^1 endpoint (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchors: Exercise 2.6.5 statement and Exercise 2.6.6 title/opening).

The variables are used together in one random sum and hence live on a common probability space; this is structural context rather than a separately stated clause (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchor: the common weighted sum in Exercises 2.6.5 and 2.6.6).
The coefficient vector is arbitrary, so the displayed inequality includes the zero vector a=0 (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchors: 'let a ... in R^N' in Exercise 2.6.5 and Exercise 2.6.6 display).

details: The claim applies to every family and every coefficient vector satisfying the inherited setting (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchors: Exercise 2.6.5 setting and Exercise 2.6.6 opening).
Once K is fixed, c(K) may not depend on N, the individual distributions, or a except through K (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchor: 'may depend only on K').
Both the lower and upper estimates are required in one two-sided inequality (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchor: Exercise 2.6.6 display).
This is specifically the p=1/L^1 case; no range of p is asserted in Exercise 2.6.6 (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchors: title 'for p = 1' and the L^1 norm in the display).
Zero means and unit variances are essential inherited hypotheses (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchor: Exercise 2.6.5 opening sentence).

The unit upper constant reflects comparison of the L^1 norm with the coefficient Euclidean norm under that normalization (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchor: right-hand inequality in Exercise 2.6.6).

The interpolation inequality ||Z||_{L^2} <= ||Z||_{L^1}^{1/4}||Z||_{L^3}^{3/4} and the p=3 appeal are a suggested proof route, not extra conclusions of the exercise (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchor: Exercise 2.6.6 Hint).

No nonzero-coefficient hypothesis appears, so a=0 is covered and makes all three displayed quantities zero (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchors: unrestricted a in Exercise 2.6.5 and the Exercise 2.6.6 display).
No exceptional distributional case or separate finite-moment hypothesis is stated beyond the inherited sub-gaussian assumptions (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchors: Exercises 2.6.5 and 2.6.6).

undebatable_constraints: The target must retain independence, sub-gaussianity, mean zero, and unit variance for every X_i (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchor: Exercise 2.6.5 setting inherited by Exercise 2.6.6).
The target must quantify arbitrary real coefficients a in R^N (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchor: Exercise 2.6.5 opening sentence).
The middle quantity must be the L^1 norm of sum_i a_i X_i (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchor: Exercise 2.6.6 display).
The comparison scale on both sides must be (sum_i a_i^2)^(1/2) (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchor: Exercise 2.6.6 display).
The upper constant must be exactly 1 (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchor: right-hand side of the Exercise 2.6.6 display).
The lower factor must be strictly positive and may depend only on K=max_i ||X_i||_{psi_2} (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchor: sentence immediately after the Exercise 2.6.6 display).
The claim must cover both inequalities, not only the lower estimate suggested by the interpolation hint (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchors: Exercise 2.6.6 display and Hint).

ambiguities.issue: The passage does not explicitly quantify N or state N>=1.

ambiguities.impact: A formalization must choose a nonempty finite index convention or otherwise define the empty-family maximum; the source itself does not prescribe the empty case.

ambiguities.issue: The source does not give a formula, monotonicity property, or explicit quantifier order for c(K).
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchor: 'c(K) > 0 is a quantity which may depend only on K.'
ambiguities.impact: The faithful content is existence/uniform availability of some strictly positive lower constant controlled only by K, not any particular numerical dependence.

ambiguities.issue: The word 'independent' is not expanded in the exercise into pairwise versus joint independence.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchor: 'Let X_1,...,X_N be independent' in Exercise 2.6.5.
ambiguities.impact: The chapter's standard probabilistic reading is independence of the family, but the selected passage supplies no separate formal definition here.

ambiguities.issue: The selected passage does not independently define L^1 or state measurability/integrability obligations.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchor: the notation ||sum_i a_i X_i||_{L^1} in the Exercise 2.6.6 display, under sub-gaussian inherited hypotheses.
ambiguities.impact: A formal target may expose routine measurability or integrability premises required by its library, but may not use them to narrow the mathematical family beyond the inherited sub-gaussian setting.

contract_plain_english: For any finite family of independent, mean-zero, unit-variance sub-gaussian real random variables X_i and any real coefficients a_i, set K=max_i ||X_i||_{psi_2}. Exercise 2.6.6 asks for a strictly positive factor c(K), uniform apart from its dependence on K, such that the L^1 norm of sum_i a_i X_i lies between c(K) times and exactly 1 times the Euclidean norm of the coefficient vector (PDF page 19; printed page 30; anchors: the inherited Exercise 2.6.5 setting and the full Exercise 2.6.6 statement).
